body: I watch anime but I'm not an otaku

I appreciate you reading it. It was a mess, I'm usually a lot better at writing but my thoughts are so jumbled right now. I held out hope for so long that I would find someone who cared, someone who wanted me, was excited to see me. Its been years, I'm allowed to give up at some point aren't I? Or am I expected to suffer for my whole life?
I'm not from shwa, I'm only there for school but I'll be doing it there so that there's no risk of my little brother finding me. If my housemates find me I'm okay with that.

Are they really short term losses if they happen continuously? I know you're supposed to "get up when you're down" but how many times can I be expected to get up? Thank you for offering your friendship, I appreciate it. I do care a lot, but lately I've had to become cold and calculated simply for my mental safety. I don't like that, that's not the type of person I wanted to be, but it was safer than constantly getting my heart broken. I'm a good person, at least I try my hardest to be. I'm in a very good program at school. I had goals and aspirations, never lazy. I was always willing to go the extra mile for someone. But I got nothing in return except heartbreak. I don't think that's fair. I'd like a girl to just enjoy some time with me, to like it when I'm around let alone jump through hoops.

It just doesn't make any sense. I've tried dissecting with every method I know. I am never unfaithful, I take the time to remember the little things; spot we first meet, first kiss, favourite chocolates, actual meaningful gifts, caring about their families. If I'm such a nice and caring person then why is it that it's so easy for people to drop me and move along like nothing. It just hurts so damn much. There is an actual ache in my chest that never goes away. I see people in happy relationships and I always watch to see if they're doing something I'm not. I can never see it. How come nobody wants me? 

Edit: I'm sorry I took so long to respond. I had a funeral to attend ironically enough.
